critical_code_review_comments: iter88.py _next_due monthly branch: replaces year/month on the datetime after already incrementing — when month wraps Dec→Jan, `year = year + 1 if month == 1 else year` runs AFTER `month = month + 1 if month < 12 else 1`, so if starting month is Dec (12), month becomes 1 and year check sees month==1 and increments — this works. But if start month is Jan (1) with candidate already <= now_ist, we'd need to go to Feb; month becomes 2, and year check `if month == 1` is False so year stays — correct. Logic OK but fragile; add a unit test.

iter88.py _attempt_payout: since Easebuzz payout creds are intentionally absent, every retry attempt will burn one of the 5 attempts and then land on 'failed'. That means enqueued items created by trigger_auto_payout will always end up 'failed' after ~9h of retries. Consider suppressing attempts when creds absent (immediate 'failed' with clear reason) or gating the loop.
iter88.py force_retry: allows retry from any state including 'succeeded' — probably not desired; should reject if status=='succeeded'.
iter88.py admin_enqueue: does not validate booking_id exists (any string accepted). Low-risk but adds noise to the queue.

iter88.py report_schedule_loop: on generation error inside the try, we don't advance next_run_at — the same schedule will be re-attempted every 15 min. Consider bumping next_run_at even on failure to avoid tight-loop retries.
iter88.py _email_report_csv opens a fresh SMTP connection per send inside the loop — fine at low volume but consider connection pooling if schedules count grows.
